transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Gamma - Head of ML), Arjun Rao (Gamma - Senior Infra Engineer), Lisa Kim (Gamma - PM)

Auto-generated summary (optional):
- Intro / company intros and qualification
- Main focus: integration surface (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy, rate limits and quotas, observability hooks)
- Action items: send security docs, LangChain examples, schedule deep-dive

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, i'm the account lead. we've got priya on the call as our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: good morning, thanks. hi all, maya here. excited to learn more about how redwood could fit into our stack.
[00:18] Lisa: hi, lisa here. product owner for our conversational platform.
[00:22] Arjun: arjun, infra. sorry for the slight delay, had one quick spin up.
[00:28] Priya: no worries. quick agenda from our side: run through your current infra and constraints, talk through integration options (sdk, langchain, llamaindex), discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private, then open up for detailed q's around quotas, proxy/gateway, observability.
[00:42] Maya: that sounds perfect. i'll quickly describe our stack. we run an in-house conversational service for customer support, about 30M monthly messages. models are currently via two vendors; we have some open-source experimentation. primary concerns are latency (<200ms p50 for short completions), data residency in eu, and PII handling. we also need tight quotas and per-route rate limiting.
[01:05] Alex: got it. that's helpful. main use cases? are you doing embeddings + retrieval or chat-only?
[01:12] Maya: both. retrieval augmented generation for support KB search (we use a vector DB) and chat flows for guided troubleshooting. embeddings pipeline is heavy: offline batch and online upserts.
[01:22] Priya: when you say vector DB, which one? and are you using LlamaIndex or LangChain in prod?
[01:27] Maya: we use Pinecone for vectors, and several teams use LangChain. a couple of experimental services use LlamaIndex.
[01:35] Priya: great — we have SDKs and example notebooks for both LangChain and LlamaIndex. quick note: sometimes transcriptions say "lang chain" or "langchain" differently but code examples should map cleanly.
[01:46] Lisa: important question: we want to put a gateway in front of calls for auth and request shaping. does redwood support running behind a proxy? we need to preserve identity headers and pass quota information.
[01:56] Alex: absolutely. most customers use a gateway/proxy pattern. you can run a reverse proxy that injects a customer-managed token or map your internal JWT to an API key. for Dedicated or Private deployments you can also terminate inside the VPC so the proxy is internal.
[02:12] Arjun: if we do hosted, do we have to expose our internal network? or can we run an edge proxy?
[02:18] Priya: hosted doesn't require network peering. you can run a lightweight gateway in your VPC that forwards requests to redwood's hosted endpoints — it's just standard HTTPS. for private deployments we support VPC peering or a private link, and for Dedicated we can do customer-dedicated pools that are accessible via private networking.
[02:36] Maya: on quotas: we need per-route quotas and token-level cost accounting. can we configure rate limits per API key or per route?
[02:45] Alex: yes — our rate limits are configurable per-API-key and per-route. the console lets you set policies and usage-based thresholds. for strict enterprise needs we offer quota guards with hard limits and alerts.
[02:57] Priya: also, we expose token-level metrics in observability — you can see token counts, latency breakdowns, and model-level cost in the Dashboard and via tracing hooks. we also ship a prometheus metrics endpoint for self-hosted/private setups.
[03:15] Arjun: prometheus endpoint — is that inside the private deploy? we prefer pulling metrics into our central cluster.
[03:21] Priya: yes, in Private and Dedicated you can host the metrics exporter inside your network. for hosted, we provide a metrics API and export options to push to customer telemetry endpoints.
[03:32] Maya: for the integration layer: we're heavy on LangChain and LlamaIndex. we'd like to see examples for retrieval + streaming responses and streaming tool calls.
[03:42] Priya: noted. we have sample notebooks: LangChain chains (retriever -> prompt template -> redwood generator) and LlamaIndex connector examples. i'll email a repo with sample streaming and function-calling examples.
[03:53] Lisa: our security checklist: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integration for key management, audit logs, and data retention controls. do you cover all that?
[04:05] Alex: yes, we have SOC 2, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC in the Console, and KMS/HSM integrations for private key storage. we also provide audit logs and configurable retention for hosted customers with enterprise add-ons. i'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:22] Maya: great. one of our stoppers is whether PII can be kept out of logs and how we manage KV cache or prefix cache — do you persist inputs?
[04:32] Priya: by default hosted endpoints keep logs for X days for ops and debugging but enterprise customers can opt out or configure redaction. for Dedicated/Private we can configure no persistence or customer-controlled retention — we also support prefix/KV cache eviction policies and in Private you can run the cache entirely in your VPC.
[04:50] Arjun: that last bit is important — we don't want KV cache hitting external network. private with cache in VPC sounds ideal if performance meets our latency goals.
[05:00] Priya: performance is a tradeoff — Dedicated with colocated GPUs tends to give best p50 latency for high QPS. we can run benchmarks but generally you see single-digit ms token throughput on optimized models but end-to-end latency depends on backend retrieval and prompt size.
[05:16] Maya: about models: we may use open models for cost reasons. does Redwood handle quantized model variants and automatic fallbacks?
[05:24] Alex: yes — the runtime supports quantized variants and we have routing policies that can fall back to compatible variants or different regions when capacity is constrained. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations on quantization profiles per workload.
[05:38] Lisa: can you explain how SDK integration works with LangChain? do we have to use HTTP or is there a native python client?
[05:46] Priya: there is a native python SDK which is used by our LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters. you can instantiate a Redwood client with api_key and call generate/stream/embed. LangChain has an official connector that plugs into the LLM and Embeddings classes. for high throughput we recommend using our batching helpers in the SDK.
[06:05] Maya: examples of batching helpers? we're currently doing manual batching in our service.
[06:10] Priya: SDK has a batch_generate endpoint and async clients which do efficient tokenization and batching on the client side before sending. on-server we also do dynamic batching. we'll include an example with asyncio and a worker pool.
[06:22] Arjun: about rate limits: if we hit a burst, will requests be throttled or queued? we can't accept big error rates from our edge.
[06:30] Alex: couple options: you can set hard limits which return 429 on breach, or soft limits with queuing and backoff. we also support priority tiers so internal critical flows can be routed to Dedicated pools with higher priority.
[06:45] Lisa: observability hooks — do you provide tracing headers we can propagate?
[06:50] Priya: yes, we support tracing correlation IDs; you can forward request IDs and we will return them in our logs and traces. we also integrate with common tracing systems and ship spans for token generation steps.
[07:02] Maya: network details: for Private deployment do you support on-prem air-gapped?
[07:08] Alex: we do offer an on-prem package for regulated workloads. that would be a separate engagement — typically full install inside the customer's network with KMS integration and no egress.
[07:18] Arjun: curious about auth flows for gateway: can we have our API gateway mint short-lived tokens for internal microservices?
[07:24] Priya: yes — short-lived tokens are supported. you can mint ephemeral keys via our token API and the SDK can authenticate with them. we also support mapping via SAML assertions for user-level RBAC.
[07:36] Maya: what's the typical onboarding timeline if we wanted Dedicated?
[07:40] Alex: for Reserved Dedicated capacity it's usually 4–8 weeks for initial capacity and network setup depending on procurement and infra readiness. Private on-prem can be longer — depends on air-gap and approvals.
[07:53] Lisa: procurement question: how do you price Dedicated vs Hosted?
[07:58] Alex: Hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings + requests). Dedicated is a reserved monthly commit for GPU capacity with overage rates. we'll send an illustrative pricing sheet after this call.
[08:08] Arjun: for compliance: do you have attestations for data residency EU-only?
[08:12] Alex: yes, we have region pinning for models and data residency controls in EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC.
[08:22] Maya: technical deep dive request: we want to validate latency and cold-start behavior for streaming responses and KV cache. can we run a poc?
[08:30] Priya: totally. a typical poc includes: 1) a small benchmark harness (we can provide), 2) sample LangChain/LlamaIndex integration, 3) a test dataset to run end-to-end retrieval + generation. we can run it against Hosted first, and then Dedicated/Private if you want network-isolated testing.
[08:48] Lisa: for the benchmark what metrics do you collect?
[08:51] Priya: p50/p90/p99 latency, token throughput, model cost per token, cache hit rate, and memory/GPU utilization. we also capture traces for each request.
[08:59] Maya: what about function calling or tool invocation? we need structured responses to drive our orchestration
[09:05] Priya: we support function/tool calling and structured output. SDK has a function_call API and streaming results include chunked json events. we'll include examples.
[09:16] Arjun: network egress for hosted: how are keys secured and rotated?
[09:20] Alex: keys are standard bearer tokens — rotation supported via the console and API; for enterprise we support KMS-backed key storage and HSM integration. tokens can be scoped and limited.
[09:30] Maya: any customers with similar scale and hybrid setup?
[09:33] Alex: we have telco customers in europe using Dedicated + Private hybrid — they use hosted for dev and dedicated for production traffic. happy to share anonymized case study.
[09:45] Lisa: are there SDK language options besides python?
[09:48] Priya: yes: python, node, and a minimal go client. wrappers for other languages exist in the community.
[09:55] Maya: latency budget reminder: 200ms p50 for short completions (under 64 tokens). can you commit to a benchmark?
[10:03] Priya: we'll run a benchmark and share numbers; generally Dedicated optimized models hit that, but end-to-end depends on retrieval flakiness. we'll instrument retrieval latency in the notebook.
[10:16] Arjun: one more infra detail: if we front with an internal gateway, can we inject headers to tag tenant and route?
[10:22] Alex: yes — we have header-based routing and you can pass tenant-id in a header; also you can pin routes to model versions.
[10:30] Maya: what's the limit on embeddings upserts? we have heavy upsert workloads and would like batch endpoints.
[10:36] Priya: embeddings have bulk upsert endpoints and async backfills. we also support batching at client side; for Dedicated you get higher throughput.
[10:45] Lisa: about observability again — can we export raw request traces to our jaeger?
[10:50] Priya: for Private/Dedicated yes; for hosted we can push traces via an integration or deliver logs to your secure S3 bucket.
[11:00] Maya: ok that covers most of our concerns. let's outline next steps.
[11:04] Alex: recap and next steps: i'll send the security pack and pricing; priya will send LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a benchmark harness; maya/team to share latency targets and sample dataset; gamma to confirm whether they'll try hosted poc first or go straight to Dedicated.
[11:18] Maya: we'll probably start with hosted poc to validate integration and then scope Dedicated for production.
[11:24] Lisa: schedule deep-dive slot for infra team — aiming for the week of Nov 20.
[11:28] Arjun: i'll confirm network topology and whether we need VPC peering or just an internal proxy.
[11:34] Alex: perfect. any final q's?
[11:37] Maya: none from me. thank you.
[11:39] Priya: thanks all — i'll follow up with the notebook and repo links.
[11:43] Alex: thanks everyone — we'll send notes and action items. have a great day.

End of transcript.
